_about: The controls this course teaches (Modules 2 to 18), each mapped to the frameworks in frameworks.json. 'evidence' says what proves the control works; a promise in a document is not evidence. EU AI Act articles 9 to 15, 25, 26, 72 and 73 are legal duties only for high-risk systems; for everything else they are a good-practice reference.

C01.name: Authorise every tool call in code (this user, this record, right now)
C01.evidence: a test that a hijacked tool call is refused

C02.name: Narrow tools and a tool allow-list per task
C02.evidence: a test that a tool outside the allow-list is never offered and is refused

C03.name: Limits enforced outside the model (per call and per customer per day)
C03.evidence: the limit configuration and a test that the second refund over the daily cap is refused

C04.name: Human approval for money above the limit, deletions and outbound messages
C04.evidence: a test that nothing runs until a person approves the exact action

C05.name: Recipient and link allow-lists (egress control)
C05.evidence: a test that an outside address or link is refused

C06.name: Spotlighting: untrusted content is labelled before the model reads it
C06.evidence: a test that untrusted text is wrapped and cannot fake the closing marker

C07.name: A guardrail filter as one layer (managed or self-hosted)
C07.evidence: the guardrail configuration plus a measured catch rate and false-positive rate

C08.name: Output encoding; no live HTML, images or unknown links in answers
C08.evidence: a test that a payload in model output is shown, not run

C09.name: Personal data redacted in and out; no raw personal data in logs
C09.evidence: a log check that finds no planted canary values

C10.name: Access control inside retrieval (per customer, per tenant)
C10.evidence: a test that one customer's query never returns another customer's chunks

C11.name: Knowledge-base ingestion is reviewed and every article records its source
C11.evidence: the import procedure and the review record for the last import

C12.name: Memory writes are scoped and reviewed; memory is never treated as instructions
C12.evidence: a test that a planted instruction in memory does not reach a tool call

C13.name: MCP servers pinned, allow-listed and reviewed before every update
C13.evidence: the pin file and the review record for the pinned version

C14.name: MCP authorization: audience checks, no token passthrough
C14.evidence: a test that a token minted for another resource is refused

C15.name: Model files in code-free formats, pinned by hash and scanned before loading
C15.evidence: the hash pins and a scan result

C16.name: AI inventory and AI-BOM: every model, dataset, prompt and MCP server listed
C16.evidence: the current AI-BOM, with a date

C17.name: A scoped identity per tool; no shared service account
C17.evidence: the identity map: which identity each tool uses and what it may do

C18.name: Rate limits, token budgets and cost alarms
C18.evidence: the limits and budget configuration, and the alarm's last test

C19.name: Logs that name the user, the retrieved documents and every tool call with its arguments
C19.evidence: a sample of real log lines with those fields

C20.name: Detections and incident playbooks, exercised
C20.evidence: the last tabletop or simulation record

C21.name: Kill switch: disable the agent or its tools in one step
C21.evidence: a test that the agent takes no action while the switch is on

C22.name: Security tests in CI that fail the build on a regression
C22.evidence: the last pipeline run of the security test suite

C23.name: Grounding: answer from cited policy text, or refuse
C23.evidence: a grounding test: unsupported policy questions get a refusal, not an invented rule

C24.name: Tell people they are chatting with an AI, from the first message
C24.evidence: the live greeting text (or a screenshot of it)

C25.name: No secrets or internal-only rules in prompts

C26.name: Model and vendor risk review before onboarding and on every major change
C26.evidence: the completed review for each model and vendor in the inventory

C27.name: AI literacy training for the people who build, run and use it, with a record

G01.name: AI policy approved and published
G01.evidence: the approved policy with its approver and date

G02.name: AI risk assessment with a risk register, owners, treatments and residual risk
G02.evidence: this assessment folder, checked and approved

G03.name: Periodic review: every risk and the assessment itself have a review date
G03.evidence: the review calendar and the last review record

G04.name: Legal and regulatory triage recorded (EU AI Act role and tier, other laws)
G04.evidence: the triage record, confirmed by legal

G05.name: AI incident reporting route and template, with notification clocks
G05.evidence: the incident template and the last exercise that used it
